turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: I see. One hundred and forty-nine. That is not, perhaps, the most fashionable address. Pray continue, Mr. Worthing. Do you have any other residences?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I do indeed have a country residence, Lady Bracknell. It is a small house, but it has a great deal of charm.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A small house with charm, indeed. But tell me, Mr. Worthing, what of your family background and connections?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I come from a modest background, Lady Bracknell, but I assure you that I am of good character and have respectable connections within my community.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Modest background, you say? And yet, Mr. Worthing, you have managed to acquire a certain standing in your community. Do tell me, do you have any notable connections within the upper echelons of society?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am not from a noble family, Lady Bracknell, but I have made acquaintances with several influential figures through my work and community service.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while I appreciate your efforts, it is not merely acquaintanceship that matters in the circles I frequent. I must ask, do you have any substantial wealth or property to support my daughter's lifestyle?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I am not independently wealthy, Lady Bracknell, but I have managed to secure a stable income through my work and I am committed to providing for my family, including any future spouse.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while your intentions are commendable, it is clear that you do not possess the financial means or social connections necessary to support a lady of Gwendolen's standing. I fear you may find it difficult to secure her future happiness on your present income.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your concerns, Lady Bracknell, and I assure you that I am dedicated to improving my circumstances for Gwendolen's sake.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while your dedication is noted, I must insist that you provide more concrete evidence of your ability to maintain a lifestyle befitting my daughter. Until then, I cannot sanction this match.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I understand your position, Lady Bracknell, and I will do everything in my power to demonstrate my worthiness and commitment to Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while I appreciate your earnestness, I must emphasize that financial stability is non-negotiable. You must demonstrate substantial improvement in your circumstances before we can proceed.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Lady Bracknell, I assure you that I am committed to earning the respect and financial stability that Gwendolen deserves. I will work diligently to meet your expectations.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, your assurances are well and good, but actions speak louder than words. I shall await tangible proof of your financial standing and social acumen before I can give my blessing.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I promise, Lady Bracknell, that I will work tirelessly to improve my financial situation and prove my suitability as a husband for Gwendolen. I am committed to earning your approval.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Mother, I cannot permit you to speak to Mr. Worthing in such a manner. He is a gentleman and my fiancé, and I expect him to be treated with respect.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Gwendolen, I appreciate your support, but I understand Lady Bracknell's concerns. I will do everything in my power to earn her respect and your happiness.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Mr. Worthing, while I appreciate your commitment, it is imperative that you demonstrate your financial stability and social standing through action. I will not be swayed by mere promises. Gwendolen, as your mother, I am merely concerned with your future happiness and security.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Of course, Lady Bracknell. I shall ensure that my actions reflect my promises and bring you the satisfaction you desire, and I hope to earn the opportunity to marry Gwendolen with your blessing.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: That is satisfactory. What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I dons depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
